meta.description: Part 2 certification pipeline bootstrap — 7 Gates, 6 Dimensions, 5 States, 33-item Gold Standard Checklist

six_dimensions.description: Build-time AI verification across 6 dimensions from P2002 §A.1; non-binding recommendations; final revision authority remains human

HIGH.definition: All dimensions consistent with authoritative sources, no ambiguity

MEDIUM.definition: One or more dimensions have minor unresolved concerns
MEDIUM.action: Flag for editorial review; do not certify

LOW.definition: Material uncertainty or contradiction with authoritative source
LOW.action: Escalate to Editorial Queue; block certification

ZERO.definition: Confirmed error (wrong answer, wrong formula, wrong authority)

escalationRules.ZERO_confidence_finding: Logged to DEFECT_LIBRARY_P2.md with new DL-P2 ID
escalationRules.two_or_more_MEDIUM: Routed to secondary human review before any certification decision

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.definition: The answer key, explanation, and distractors are consistent with the authoritative standard governing the tested concept
part2Authorities: FASB ASC (ratio definitions, financial statement presentation)
IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice (4 standards)
blockingConditions: Answer key contradicts authoritative standard
Formula selected is incorrect for the concept
Formula inputs not traceable to stem/exhibit data
Authority citation mismatches concept (e.g., ASC 450 cited for CAPM)
dimensions.verificationMethod: Independent derivation of correct answer from stem + choices; cross-reference authority against P2002 §E.2 authority-verification table

dimensions.name: Precision
dimensions.definition: The fact pattern yields exactly one defensible answer; no missing assumptions, no contradictory data
part2SpecificConcerns: Missing tax rate in WACC calculation
Ambiguous treatment of operating vs. finance leases under ASC 842
Unstated assumption about market values vs. book values for WACC weights
blockingConditions: Fact pattern yields more than one defensible answer
Missing critical input data not derivable from context
Stem data contradicts exhibit data
Question is unanswerable without external knowledge not stated
dimensions.verificationMethod: Solve independently from stem + exhibits only; verify single answer emerges; check all inputs are stated or derivable

dimensions.name: DifficultyCalibration
dimensions.definition: The cognitive demand implied by the LOS is consistent with the question's stated difficulty and Bloom's level per domain targets (P2002 §G)
blockingConditions: Apply at Easy difficulty — flag
Evaluate at Easy difficulty — auto-reject
Definition-match inflation (Moderate label on Remember/Understand item) — DL-031 pattern
Difficulty label does not match cognitive demand of the stem
dimensions.verificationMethod: Cross-check Difficulty/DifficultyScore against CognitiveLevel and stem complexity; verify Bloom's level alignment per domain targets

dimensions.name: DistractorEngineering
dimensions.definition: Each distractor maps to a real misconception or plausible calculation path; every distractor represents a documented exam trap or known student error
part2ExampleTraps: Using after-tax cost of debt twice in WACC
Omitting preferred stock component in WACC
Using historical market return instead of expected in CAPM
Using book values instead of market values for WACC weights
Omitting working capital recovery in terminal year NPV
Mixing variable cost per unit with total fixed costs in CVP
Not adjusting for multi-product sales mix in breakeven
Forgetting opportunity cost in transfer price when capacity is full
blockingConditions: Any distractor is obviously wrong (no plausible path to that answer)
Two distractors test the same misconception (redundant)
All distractors are implausible or guessable
dimensions.verificationMethod: Map each distractor to a specific candidate error path; verify distinctness across all pairs; verify each distractor text addresses its specific error

dimensions.name: BlueprintAlignment
dimensions.definition: The LOSTag, Topic, and cognitive level align with a specific Part 2 Content Specification Outline learning outcome
blockingConditions: No LOSTag present or LOSTag maps to Part 1 CSO
Topic does not align with claimed domain
Cognitive level inconsistent with LOS depth verb
Part field is not 2
dimensions.verificationMethod: Verify LOSTag against P2001 Appendix A; verify Topic, Section, and BlueprintDomain are consistent; verify Part field = 2

dimensions.name: Part2Relevance
dimensions.definition: The question tests Part 2 material; no concept, standard, or calculation belongs exclusively to Part 1
part1Exclusives: Standard costing variances (DM, DL, VOH, FOH)
Joint product cost allocation (NRV, physical measures)
permittedOverlap: CVP analysis / breakeven (tests at higher Bloom's levels: Analyze/Evaluate in Part 2 vs. Apply in Part 1)
Ethical principles (deeper application in Part 2: FCPA, SOX, IMA decision model)
blockingConditions: Item tests a Part 1 exclusive as its primary concept
No clear Part 2 domain association
Domain boundary violation (Part 2 item mislabeled as Part 1 domain)
dimensions.verificationMethod: Check topic against Part 1 Exclusives list; verify Part2OnlyFlag is true (structural gate); verify Domain A-F is a Part 2 domain

seven_gates.description: 7-step certification pipeline from P2002 §D; every question must pass all gates before reaching Production

gates.name: Technical Review
criticalChecks: Correct answer verified against governing Part 2 authority
Formula selection correct for concept tested
All formula inputs traceable to question stem data
Authority citation matches the concept (no ASC 450 cited for CAPM)
No Part 1-only concept tested as primary
Domain boundary respected
Part2OnlyFlag: true confirmed as appropriate
part2Specific: Domain A authorities: FASB ASC, IFRS, SEC reporting standards
Domain B authorities: CAPM, Modigliani-Miller, Basel III, FX/IFRS
Domain C authorities: IMA SMA on relevant costing, managerial economics
Domain D authorities: COSO ERM 2017, ISO 31000
Domain E authorities: NPV/IRR theory, MACRS (IRS Pub 946), real options
Domain F authorities: IMA Ethics, SOX 2002, FCPA, Dodd-Frank

gates.name: Psychometric Review
criticalChecks: Difficulty score matches item's actual cognitive demand
Bloom's level aligned with difficulty (Evaluate at Easy = auto-reject)
Distractor plausibility: each wrong option represents a specific misconception
No cueing: no grammatical, length, or position cues to correct answer
Answer balance: per-section correct-answer distribution within 22-28% per position
No running pattern: no streak of same CC position longer than 4 consecutive items
Definition-match inflation checked (Moderate items that are Easy → DL-031)

gates.name: Numerical Validation
criticalChecks: Independent recalculation matches stored Correct value
Formula selection correct (P2002 §E.1 formula inventory — 40+ formulas)
Input traceability: every numerical input traces to stem/exhibit
Unit consistency verified
Rounding policy followed (P2002 §D.4 — rounding table)
Within accepted tolerance (P2002 §D.4 — tolerance table)
Part 2-specific common errors checked (WACC: pre-tax vs after-tax, DuPont: avg vs end-of-period equity, NPV: working capital recovery)
recalculationProtocol: Read stem and exhibits (not stored Correct value)

gates.name: Instructional Review
criticalChecks: EV1: Minimum 50 characters per explanation field
EV2: No placeholder phrases
EV3: Correct answer references Part 2 governing authority by name
EV4: Distractor explanations are choice-specific (not identical across slots)
EV5: Formula numbers in explanation match exhibit/stem values
EV6: Arithmetic result matches Correct value
EV7: No uncertain language
EV8: ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] === "" (DL-008 compliant)

part2ExplanationTemplates.calculationCorrect: The correct answer is [letter/number]. [Formula with substituted values] = [result]. Under [Part 2 authority], the rule is [key requirement]. In context, [business interpretation]. A common error is to [specific trap].
part2ExplanationTemplates.calculationDistractor: Option [letter] incorrectly [specific error]. A candidate reaching this answer likely [likely mistake]. The correct approach is [contrast with correct method].
part2ExplanationTemplates.conceptualCorrect: The correct answer is [letter] because [reasoning]. Under [Part 2 framework], [key rule]. In practice, this means [business interpretation].
part2ExplanationTemplates.conceptualDistractor: Option [letter] [restate choice]. This is incorrect because [specific error]. The misconception is that [what candidate thinks], but [correct concept].

gates.name: Metadata Review
criticalChecks: All required fields present (P2002 §D.6 — field table)
Part field === 2
Section in {A, B, C, D, E, F}
QuestionID matches format P2-{Section}-{NNN}
question_state in {Unprocessed, In Audit, Editorial Queue, Certified, Archived}
Difficulty in {Easy, Moderate-Easy, Moderate, Difficult, Very Difficult}
DifficultyScore: integer 1-5
CognitiveLevel in {Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate}
CalculationItem: boolean
Part2OnlyFlag: MUST be true (strict boolean check — rejects absent, false, "true" string, 1 number)
Part2OnlyFlag survives JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(item)) round-trip
part2OnlyFlagProtocol: 1. Verify Part2OnlyFlag field exists in JSON object
Any check fails → BLOCK certification for this item

gates.name: Final Validation
criticalChecks: All G1-G5 gates passed
Automated validation suite runs with zero errors
Zero new warnings from baseline
Governance guard all rules PASS
grep -c '"QuestionID"' count matches registry for target pack
Pack file parses cleanly via JSON.parse() or Function constructor
No detectable DL-008, DL-026, or DL-013 pattern in certification batch
Part2OnlyFlag verified on every certified item

gates.name: Approval
criticalChecks: G1-G6 all passed with documented evidence
All gate reports filed in reports/
REVISION_HISTORY.md entry written with before/after counts
DEFECT_LIBRARY_P2.md updated if any defects found
CURRENT_BASELINES_P2.md updated with new hashes
Pre-delivery safety check confirms 0 known-defective QIDs in delivery pool
All items in batch carry Part2OnlyFlag: true

five_states.description: Governance states for every Part 2 item from P2002 §B.1-B.5

states.description: Not yet audited; initial authoring state. Item exists in pack file with full content but has not entered certification pipeline.
states.exitRule: Transitions to In Audit upon entry into a sub-batch (auditor selection)
states.blockingConditions: None — this is the initial state

states.description: Currently under review in a sub-batch. Item is undergoing six-dimension AI verification and gate-level review.
states.entryRule: Explicit selection into a certification sub-batch from Unprocessed or Editorial Queue
exitTransitions: In Audit → Certified: HIGH-confidence six-dimension AI verification + user approval (all 7 conditions met per §B.3)
In Audit → Editorial Queue: structural or content revision required
In Audit → Unprocessed: (not a valid transition — use Editorial Queue)
states.blockingConditions: Cannot transition to Certified if any certification-blocking condition exists (§B.4)

states.description: Requires structural or content revision before re-audit. Item has been reviewed and found to need changes that the auditor cannot apply directly.
states.entryRule: From In Audit when structural/content revision is required
states.exitRule: Transitions back to In Audit after revisions are applied and the item is re-entered into a sub-batch
states.blockingConditions: Cannot transition directly to Certified — must pass through In Audit first

states.description: Passed HIGH-confidence six-dimension verification + user approval. Eligible for learner practice sessions.
entryRequirements: Six-dimension AI verification produces HIGH confidence across all 6 dimensions
Distractor tier map (A/B/C/D) recorded in certification entry
All low-confidence claims resolved and documented
All three non-CC ExplanationWrong slots confirmed non-empty (≥50 chars each, DL-026 compliance)
states.exitRule: Certified → In Audit only via explicit re-verification request (requires: specific defect finding logged to DEFECT_LIBRARY_P2.md, user authorization for status change, REVISION_HISTORY.md entry documenting reversion)
states.blockingConditions: Cannot be downgraded without documented re-verification request (§B.5)

states.description: Removed from active pool (content preserved). Item is excluded from learner delivery but retained in pack file.
states.entryRule: From any state; consolidation or removal from active pool
states.exitRule: Can be restored to Unprocessed if re-activated (content preserved — only state field changes)
states.blockingConditions: Archived items must retain full content; only question_state field changes. Rollback logs maintained in reports/.

five_states.transitionDiagram: Unprocessed → In Audit → Certified ✓; In Audit → Editorial Queue → In Audit → Certified ✓; Any State → Archived

gold_standard_checklist.description: 33 distinct checklist items from P2002 §F; 21 MCQ + 12 Case-Study-Specific

mcqChecklist.item: Blueprint alignment — Question maps to a specific Part 2 IMA Learning Outcome Statement (P2001 Appendix A)
Technical accuracy — Accounting/finance treatment is correct under current Part 2 authorities (ASC, CAPM, COSO ERM 2017, IMA Ethics, SOX, FCPA)
Numerical accuracy — All calculations independently verified via Formula Verification Protocol (§E.1)
Correct answer — The stored CorrectChoice matches independent expert judgment
Distractor plausibility — Every distractor represents a realistic candidate misconception
Distractor discrimination — No distractor is obviously wrong; each targets a distinct error
No cueing — No grammatical, length, or position cues point to the correct answer
Answer balance — The question does not create a pattern if combined with adjacent questions
Explanation — authority — Correct answer explanation names the governing Part 2 standard/authority
Explanation — solution — Shows formula with substituted values (calculations) or reasoning chain (conceptual)
Explanation — business context — Interprets the result in the scenario
Explanation — distractors — Each wrong-choice explanation is specific and teaches why it is wrong
Explanation — exam trap — Identifies at least one common candidate error
Business realism — Scenario uses realistic business language, not textbook phrasing
Writing clarity — No grammatical errors; professional tone
Accessibility — No biased language; fair to all candidate populations
Metadata complete — All required fields present and valid (§D.6)
Metadata cross-references — Formula references and authority references resolve correctly
Part2OnlyFlag — Field present and true (§E.4)
Domain boundary — Question does not test Part 1-exclusive concepts as primary material (§E.3)
Validation pass — Automated validation suite passes with zero errors (§D.7)

caseStudySpecificChecklist.item: Scenario realism — Named company, stakeholder, business trigger, and clear task present
Exhibit quality — Professional format, no decorative data (§C.3)
Data consistency — Numbers in exhibits are internally consistent (§C.6)
Question interconnection — Items follow logical progression (calculate → analyze → decide)
Cognitive progression — Items progress from lower to higher Bloom's levels (§C.4)
Independent answerability — Each item can be answered without relying on correct answers to prior items (§C.5)
Exhibit referencing — Every exhibit is referenced by at least one item
Data consumption — Every exhibit row/column is consumed by at least one item
Case-level metadata — All required case-level fields present and valid (§D.6)
Item-level metadata — All required item-level fields present and valid (§D.6)
Exhibit-level metadata — ExhibitID, Purpose, and ReferencedBy fields present
Difficulty calibration — Case-level difficulty is within ±1 of mean item difficulty

gold_standard_checklist.goldStandardDefinition: 100/100 on rubric + every checklist item satisfied + reviewed by 2 independent reviewers (1 accounting, 1 editorial) + all numerical content verified by 2 separate calculations + complete metadata with no warnings + Part2OnlyFlag: true verified by all 7 gates

correctChoiceDistribution.note: Strong B-bias (40.0%). CorrectChoice B is significantly overrepresented. This is a systematic issue — items CC=A/D are underrepresented. For a 500-item pool, this distribution may need strategic rebalancing.

Difficult_4.status: FAIL — 70% Difficult vs 30% target for Domain A

difficultyDistribution.note: CRITICAL CONCERN: All 30 items are Difficult or Very Difficult. Zero items at Easy, Moderate-Easy, or Moderate. This is a severe difficulty distribution mismatch. The first 30 items skew extremely hard and do not represent the target distribution for a 500-item pool. Subsequent authoring waves must prioritize Easy (1), Moderate-Easy (2), and Moderate (3) items to restore balance.

cognitiveLevelDistribution.note: CRITICAL CONCERN: All 30 items are Analyze or Evaluate — the two highest cognitive levels. Zero items at Remember, Understand, or Apply. This is a severe Bloom's distribution mismatch. For Domain A, the targets are Remember 10%, Understand 20%, Apply 45%, Analyze 20%, Evaluate 5%. Current sample: Analyze 53.3%, Evaluate 46.7%. Subsequent authoring waves must prioritize Apply-level calculation items (45% per-domain target) and lower-level items.

calculationItemDistribution.note: 4 items (P2-A-010, P2-A-021, P2-A-024, P2-A-028) are purely conceptual/judgment. The remaining 26 require computation. This is consistent with Domain A (Financial Statement Analysis) which is calculation-intensive.

criticalItems.issue: Drafting notes embedded in ExplanationCorrect and VerificationChecks fields
criticalItems.details: The ExplanationCorrect text contains authoring work-in-progress notes including 'Let me re-derive...', 'Ugh, I made an error...', 'I need to fix...', 'I'll start fresh...'. The VerificationChecks field similarly contains drafting commentary. These are not learner-safe — they expose the item's internal construction process and contain self-critical language ('I made an error').
criticalItems.remediationRequired: Rewrite ExplanationCorrect as a clean, professional explanation. Clean VerificationChecks. The underlying math (normalized NPM = 6.73%) is correct — only the presentation needs fixing.

cosmeticIssues.issue: Dollar amounts use $27.6M vs $27,600,000 notation — consistent within item but differs from some peer items

estimatedTimeToFirstCertification.note: The primary bottleneck is the difficulty/cognitive distribution gap. All 30 existing items are at the Difficult+ / Analyze+ end. A certification wave that only certifies these items would create a learner pool with an 100% hard-skew — violating P2002 §G targets. The fastest path to first certification is to (1) fix P2-A-017, (2) build infrastructure, (3) author a balanced 30-50 item wave with proper difficulty/Bloom's distribution, (4) certify that balanced wave as the first batch.
